angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 206.19 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.8500 +/- 0.0216 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 206.19 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 +/- 0.1 solar radii from Jankowski et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260901721J/abstract): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.07 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Jankowski et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260901721J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5858 +/- 26 K from Jankowski et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260901721J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jankowski et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-223 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260901721J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-223.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.425, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
